pass_a_gloss: They had also and the Egyptian magicians rods, which they wanted to use they wanted to refute Moses and Aaron as not from God. But the rods of the sophists and magicians are overturned by those from God; for the rod of Aaron swallowed them, for it was sufficient for this even without the rod of Moses. 'Thus struck Jeremiah the prophet' said Pashur, and according to custom, 'and struck Jeremiah the prophet.' Then follows 'the prophet.' Here then the one striking Jeremiah the prophet struck. It is written moreover in the Acts that someone struck Paul by command of Ananias the high priest. Therefore Paul said: 'God will strike you, you whitewashed wall.' And until now, by unlawful high priest, the Ebionite sailors order the apostle Jesus Christ to be struck with slanderous words. And Paul says to such a high priest word: 'God will strike you.' And such a high priest is superficially handsome and a whitewashed wall, 'I have given my back to stripes,' and Christ says: 'My back I have given to stripes, my cheeks to smitings, my face I have not turned away from shame of spittings.' These the innocent know only for that time, when Pilate scourged him, when the Jews conspired against him. But I see Jesus daily giving his back to stripes. Enter into the synagogues of the Jews, and see Jesus by them with the tongue of blasphemy being scourged. See those gathered from the nations, conspiring against Christians, how they take Jesus, and there he gives his own back to stripes. Consider the word of God being insulted, maligned, hated by the unbelievers. See that he gave his cheeks to smitings, and having taught that if anyone strikes you on the cheek, turn the other also, he himself does this. So many strike and scourge him, and he is silent and does not speak. For it is written: not speaking while being scourged. And the face of Jesus even until now he has not turned away from shame of spittings. Who among those despising the doctrine does not, as it were, spit upon Jesus enduring until now?

pass_b_english: The enchanters of the Egyptians also had rods that wanted to refute the rods of Moses and Aaron as not being from God. But the rods from God overturn those of the sophists and enchanters; 'Aaron’s swallowed them'—for it alone was enough for this even without Moses’ rod. So then Pashhur 'struck Jeremiah the prophet,' and with character: 'and he struck Jeremiah the prophet.' (Isaiah 50:6) 'The prophet' is also added. Here then the one who struck struck Jeremiah the prophet.

And it is written in Acts that someone struck Paul, ordered by Ananias the high priest. Therefore Paul said: 'God is about to strike you, whitewashed wall.' (Matthew 5:39) And until now Ebionites, ordered by an unlawful high-priestly word, strike the apostle of Jesus Christ with blasphemous words. And Paul says toward such a high-priestly word: 'God is about to strike you.' And such a high priest is handsome on the surface and a whitewashed wall.

Christ says: 'I have given my back to scourges, and my cheeks to blows, and I did not turn my face away from the shame of spit.' (Isaiah 53:7) The simple know these things only of that time when Pilate scourged him, when Jews planned against him. But I see Jesus daily 'giving his back to scourges.' Go into the synagogues of the Jews and see Jesus scourged by them with the tongue of blasphemy. See those gathered from the nations planning against Christians, how they take Jesus, and there too he 'gives his own back to scourges.' Consider the Word of God being insulted, spoken ill of, hated by the unbelievers. See that 'he gave his cheeks to blows,' and having taught that if someone strikes you on the cheek turn also the other, he himself does it. So many strike and scourge him, and he is silent and does not speak. For it is written that he does not speak when being scourged. And 'until now Jesus has not turned his face away from the shame of spit.'
